objective: Calculate the six trigonometric ratios where defined and explain each undefined value using a zero denominator.

sources.title: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 7.4 The Other Trigonometric Functions
sources.use: Scope and optional reading. Instruction, examples, questions and diagrams are original; every domain and sign is checked from the coordinate definitions.

instructionOutline: Define the six functions from a terminal point
Distinguish tangent from cotangent
Pair each function with its reciprocal
Normalize a non-unit point
Choose signs before calculating
Evaluate exact special and coterminal angles
Separate a zero numerator from a zero denominator
Build the four axis rows
State domains with all excluded angles
Check the ranges of the six functions
Distinguish reciprocals from inverse functions
Read negative powers and calculator labels
Recover all ratios from sine or cosine
Recover a point from secant or cosecant
Recover a direction from tangent or cotangent
Check whether the given information is sufficient
Derive the two additional squared identities
Preserve domain restrictions when simplifying
Explain even and odd behavior
Explain why the periods differ
Test a claimed period with more than one point
Audit calculator output near an excluded angle

checkpointPolicy.pass: Every part of all four questions must be correct without hints.
checkpointPolicy.sampling: Every form requires all six ratios reconstructed from one given ratio and a quadrant, all six values at an axis with a zero-denominator explanation, a reciprocal compared with a principal inverse, and both parity and period reasoning. The four questions sample the broader practice coverage rather than certify every variant separately.
checkpointPolicy.assistedWork: Guided work, investigation and practice do not award independent evidence.

generatorRules: Accept exact rational and radical equivalence. Use a distinct undefined answer state, never infinity, a sentinel number or a tolerance around zero.
Use the coordinate definitions sin=y/r, cos=x/r, tan=y/x, cot=x/y, sec=r/x and csc=r/y, with r positive. Reject the origin.
Normalize exactly and preserve every signed coordinate. A denominator is zero only when it equals zero exactly.
Include all four quadrants, all four axes, negative and coterminal angles, irrational values and large finite ratios.
For reconstruction in an open quadrant, validate range, sign and nonzero coordinates before selecting a root. A lone ratio without a sign condition may be ambiguous.
Treat cot=x/y as the definition. The expression 1/tan has a smaller domain and does not supply cotangent at a vertical-axis point.
State the principal inverse range in notation questions and keep angle outputs separate from dimensionless reciprocals.
Require original-domain conditions in quotient simplifications and the two derived Pythagorean identities.
Use fundamental periods pi for tangent/cotangent and 2pi for sine/cosine/secant/cosecant, on their domains. Equal values at one pair of inputs do not establish a period.
Cosine and secant are even; sine, tangent, cosecant and cotangent are odd. An odd function need not have zero in its domain.
Shuffle choice options deterministically, retain immutable question snapshots and reject unknown families or variants.

workflow: Choose one of six terminal points or type real exact coordinates whose squared radius is rational.
Predict which of tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant are defined by inspecting the appropriate coordinate denominator.
Calculate all six values, typing undefined where needed.
Compare the normalized point, labeled diagram and accessible table of each formula, exact denominator and value.
Compare reflection, a half-turn and a full turn using a second exact table; justify both a zero-denominator decision and the shorter tangent/cotangent period.
Clear dependent answers and feedback whenever the inputs, case or predictions change.
investigation.scope: Coordinates are bounded in magnitude by 100 and must yield a nonzero radius supported by the exact radical parser. These are tool limits, not restrictions on trigonometric functions.
investigation.accessibility: Labeled native inputs, keyboard controls, explicit undefined text, exact table alternatives, live feedback, a focusable scroll region and mobile layout checks.
